stem: The diagram shows Chirag's and Leela's square dosas of the same whole size. Chirag cuts his into $3$ equal pieces. Leela cuts hers into $3$ pieces of different sizes. Each takes one piece and calls it one-third of the dosa.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides whose piece is a valid one-third?

options.text: Only Chirag's piece is one-third, because the whole was split into equal-size parts.
Both pieces are one-third, because each person took one of three pieces.
Calling a piece one-third is what forces the dosa cuts to be equal.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A fractional unit needs equal-size parts of the identified whole; only Chirag's equal cuts give a true one-third.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal-size partitioning of the whole makes a valid unit fraction. Counting three pieces of any size omits equal size. Saying the name creates equal cuts reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as two squares: equal thirds vs unequal thirds.
